style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of tears and sheaves -- a Song of Ascents in two tenses. The first half remembers a restoration so sudden it felt unreal: when the LORD turned Zion's captivity, we were like men dreaming; mouths filled with laughter, tongues with ringing song, and even the watching nations conceded the verdict -- 'the LORD has done great things for them.' The second half prays from a harder present: restore us AGAIN, LORD, like the streams in the Negev -- the desert wadis that lie bone-dry until the winter rains send water roaring down them in a day. Between remembered joy and requested joy stands the psalm's great law of the harvest: those who sow in tears will reap with ringing cries. The final picture is drawn in a single continuous motion -- the sower walking out weeping, scattering seed he can barely spare into ground that shows nothing, and the same man coming back, coming back with rejoicing, his arms full of sheaves. It is the farmer's promise for every discouraged parent, evangelist, intercessor, and laborer: tears do not disqualify the sowing; in God's field they water it.

1.text: A song of ascents. When the LORD turned back the captivity of Zion, we were like men in a dream.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. When the LORD [YHWH] turned again ['returned the returning', shub, the KJV margin] the captivity [shibah] of Zion [Tsiyyon], we were like them that dream [chalam].
1.notes: The Hebrew doubles the return: be-shub YHWH et-shibat -- when the LORD returned the returning (H7725), restoration so complete the language folds over itself. chalam (H2492): joy past believing, pinch-yourself grace -- the exiles walking home from Babylon unsure they were awake (cf. Ezra 1; Acts 12:9, Peter thinking he saw a vision).

2.text: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with ringing song; then they said among the nations, 'The LORD has done great things for them.'
2.amp: Then was our mouth [peh] filled [male] with laughter [sechok], and our tongue [lashon] with singing [rinnah -- ringing cries]: then said [amar] they among the heathen [goy], 'The LORD [YHWH] has done great things ['hath magnified to do with them', gadal, the KJV margin] for them.'
2.notes: sechok (H7814), the laughter Ecclesiastes audited and Sarah named her son for, here filled (male, H4390) to the brim legitimately -- and the most reliable witnesses testify: the goyim themselves, the watching nations, credit YHWH by name. God's kindness to His people is His advertisement among their neighbors (cf. Joshua 2:10-11).

3.text: Great things the LORD has done for us -- and we are glad.
3.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has done [asah] great things [gadal] for us; whereof we are glad [sameach].
3.notes: The church takes the nations' sentence and signs it: what they said about us, we say to Him. gadal (H1431), magnified doing -- and the response is almost understated: sameach (H8056), glad. Some testimonies need no elaboration, only ownership.

4.text: Turn our captivity again, O LORD, like the streambeds in the Negev.
4.amp: Turn again [shub] our captivity [shebut -- our fortunes], O LORD [YHWH], as the streams [aphiq -- the wadis, the channel-beds] in the south [Negev -- the dry southland].
4.notes: The tense shifts and the psalm becomes ours: shub again, LORD -- restoration remembered becomes restoration requested; yesterday's miracle is today's argument. The aphiqim (H650) of the Negev (H5045) are the image: dead-dry channels that one winter storm turns to rivers in an hour. Pray for water where only the riverbed exists.

5.text: Those who sow in tears will reap with ringing cries of joy.
5.amp: They that sow [zara] in tears [dimah] shall reap [qatsar] in joy ['singing', rinnah, the KJV margin].
5.notes: The law of the harvest, stated as flat promise: zara (H2232) done weeping still counts as sowing -- tears do not void the seed. And the exchange rate is fixed by God: dimah in, rinnah (H7440) out; the crying at planting becomes the ringing at qatsar (H7114). Paul's version: he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully (cf. 2 Corinthians 9:6; Galatians 6:9).

6.text: The one who goes out, going out in tears, carrying the bag of precious seed, will surely come in -- come in with ringing joy, carrying his sheaves with him.
6.amp: He that goes forth [halak] and weeps [bakah], bearing [nasa] precious seed ['seed basket', meshek zera, the KJV margin], shall doubtless come [bo] again with rejoicing [rinnah], bringing [nasa] his sheaves [alummah] with him.
6.notes: The promise slowed to a single walking figure, with the Hebrew doubling both journeys: going he goes weeping, coming he comes with rinnah. The meshek zera (H2233) is seed a hungry man could have eaten -- sowing as costly faith. And both trips carry: nasa (H5375) the seed out, nasa the alummot (H485) home; nothing scattered for God comes back empty (cf. Isaiah 55:10-11; John 12:24).
